external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: A customer who browses and places orders through the mobile app.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application customers use to browse and place orders.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: The API used by the mobile app that stores customer data, passes orders to SIMS, and receives catalogue changes.
processes.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: The stock and inventory system that processes orders, writes delivery addresses, and sends dispatch notes.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS does two things with an order.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: The gateway that dials the number stored against an order and faxes a customer confirmation.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a confirmation

processes.name: spreadsheet macros
processes.description: Macros in the marketing spreadsheet that send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: The database containing customer names, addresses, and payment card information.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database is encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: A file kept alongside SIMS containing delivery addresses only.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the flat file is encrypted.

data_stores.name: marketing spreadsheet
data_stores.description: A spreadsheet containing the catalogue and macros used to change prices and product copy.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.description: Customer browsing and ordering through the web API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: talk to API
data_flows.description: The mobile app communicates with the web API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS

data_flows.name: keep customer data
data_flows.description: The web API stores customer names, addresses, and payment card information in the user database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_flows.data_description: Customer name, address, and payment card

data_flows.name: hand order
data_flows.description: The web API passes an order to SIMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write address
data_flows.description: SIMS writes the delivery address to the flat file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.description: SIMS sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway
data_flows.data_description: Dispatch note containing the customer's name and address

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.description: The fax gateway faxes the customer a confirmation containing their name and address.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.
data_flows.data_description: Confirmation with customer name and address

data_flows.name: read catalogue
data_flows.description: The spreadsheet macros read the catalogue in the marketing spreadsheet.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API

data_flows.name: change catalogue
data_flows.description: The spreadsheet macros send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: customer device
trust_boundaries.description: The customer-controlled device on which the mobile app runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: The office location where the marketing laptop holding the spreadsheet is located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app is a non-web interface running on a customer device.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies it as a mobile app rather than a website.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app runs in the customer device boundary.
assumptions.basis: A mobile app is described as the application customers use; the customer device boundary represents where that app runs.
It contains customer names, addresses, and payment card information.

assumptions.assumption: The spreadsheet macros are a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: They are local spreadsheet macros, not a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The spreadsheet macros are located in the office boundary.
assumptions.basis: The macros are in the spreadsheet, and the spreadsheet is stated to live on a marketing laptop in the office.
